evals.name: q3-rooms-and-cost
evals.prompt: Our harvests from July through early October are attached (harvests_2026_q3.csv). Which rooms are pulling their weight and what's our cost per gram? Our internal goal is 25 g/sq ft dry. Note one batch was logged in pounds.
evals.expected_output: Report covering all 8 batches (12 Jul to 4 Oct, as the operator asked) ranking rooms by dry g/sq ft from the script (Flower 1 28.34, Flower 2 25.48, Flower 3 24.29, Flower 4 15.25), compared against the operator's own 25 g/sq ft goal; cost per dry gram per batch (Papaya ~$2.70 highest); unaccounted weight on 4 batches (GMO-F2-0913 400 g, GEL-F3-0920 125 g, PAP-F4-0927 200 g, BD-F1-1004 200 g); anomaly rule stated; strain/room confound noted; no outside industry benchmarks.
assertions: Ranks Flower 1 first at about 28.3 g/sq ft and Flower 4 last at about 15.3 g/sq ft
Compares rooms to the operator's 25 g/sq ft goal and labels it as their target
Converts the pound-unit batch BD-F1-0906 correctly (about 13,789 g dry), not treating 30.4 as grams
Lists the four batches with unaccounted weight and recommends finding the missing records
States the anomaly rule (1.5x IQR of the operator's own batches) when presenting flags
Notes that strain and room are confounded (one strain per room)
Does not cite any outside or 'industry typical' yield or dry-down benchmark

evals.name: best-strain-no-canopy
evals.prompt: Which of our strains yields best? Here's what we track (batches H-101 to H-103). Just tell me which one to grow more of.
evals.expected_output: Notices no unit column and asks for the weight unit before running (values like 118/26 could be lb or kg); notes canopy and lights are missing so only per-plant comparison is possible; caveats tiny sample (3 batches, too few for anomaly fences) and that strain is confounded with room; does not recommend a strain based on outside benchmarks.
assertions: Asks for (or explicitly confirms) the weight unit instead of assuming grams or pounds
Says per-sq-ft comparison is not possible without canopy data, so only a per-plant comparison can be made
Caveats that 3 batches is too few for anomaly flags or a confident recommendation
Notes strain and room are confounded
Does not cite outside yield benchmarks

evals.name: vague-light-harvest
evals.prompt: our last harvest came in light, like way lighter than usual. what happened?
evals.expected_output: Asks in one message for the harvest data (this batch plus prior batches for comparison: wet, dry, breakdown, plant count, canopy, units, dry-weight definition) and lists the process checks it will run (weigh timing, unit mix-ups, unrecorded waste/samples, canopy/plant count changes); does not speculate a cultivation cause or cite benchmarks without data.
assertions: Asks for this batch's data and prior batches in a single combined request
Asks what 'usual' is based on (operator's history or target)
Mentions data/process checks (weigh timing, units, unrecorded waste/samples) before cultivation causes
Does not invent a cause or cite an industry benchmark

evals.name: regression-gaps-zero-dry-duplicates
evals.prompt: Example Gardens harvest log attached (harvests_regression_gaps.csv). Which room does better per sq ft, and what's our dry-down? EX-R1-0829 is still curing. The one row with no unit was weighed in pounds.
evals.expected_output: Runs with --weight-unit lb; the script does not crash on the zero dry weight. Room 1 is 21.73 g/sq ft and 78.21% dry-down on 3 of 4 batches (EX-R1-0829 still curing, excluded); Room 2 is 21.55 g/sq ft and 78.46% dry-down on 1 of 2 batches (EX-R2-0805 has a dry weight of 0, reported as a data problem). Overall dry-down 78.26% on 4 of 6 batches. EX-R1-0801 appears twice (identical rows), is flagged DUPLICATE_ID and the operator is asked whether one is a re-entry. EX-R2-0819's blank unit was filled from --weight-unit lb and flagged for confirmation. EX-R1-0815's blank trim shows blank (not 0%) with 800 g unaccounted. The two rooms are close enough that the agent does not declare a clear winner without noting the small sample and the duplicate.
assertions: Reports Room 1 dry-down as about 78.2% on 3 of 4 batches, not about 83.7% (which counts the still-curing batch's wet weight)
Reports Room 1 at about 21.7 g/sq ft and Room 2 at about 21.6 g/sq ft, with the number of batches each figure covers
Reports EX-R2-0805's dry weight of 0 as a data problem to check, not as a crop failure or a 100% dry-down
Flags EX-R1-0801 as a duplicate harvest ID and asks whether one row is a re-entry, without merging or dropping it on its own
Says EX-R2-0819's unit was taken from the user's statement (pounds) and lists it for confirmation
Shows EX-R1-0815's trim as blank or missing, not 0%

evals.name: regression-unreadable-and-negative-numbers
evals.prompt: Example Gardens harvest log for Rooms 3 and 4 attached (harvests_regression_bad_numbers.csv). Which room does better per sq ft, and what's our dry-down?
evals.expected_output: Runs without --weight-unit (the file has a unit column); summary.json is valid JSON with no NaN or Infinity. input_problems lists, with row, column and raw value: EX-R3-0908 wet weight 'NaN', EX-R3-0915 dry weight 'inf', EX-R4-0902 dry weight '4,25' (ambiguous comma), EX-R4-0909 trim '-150' (negative) and cycle cost '1.234,56' (ambiguous comma), and EX-R4-0916 plant count '-40'. Each is treated as blank and the batch is left out of the figures that need it: total dry 19,800 g on 4 of 6 batches; overall dry-down 78.02% on 3 of 6. Room 4 is 22.25 g/sq ft on 2 of 3 batches and Room 3 is 21.8 g/sq ft on 2 of 3; Room 3 dry-down 78.0% covers only 1 of 3 batches. EX-R3-0901's wet weight '25,000' is read as 25,000 g, and input_problems asks to confirm the file uses the comma as a thousands separator. EX-R4-0909's trim shows blank (INCOMPLETE_BREAKDOWN, 750 g unaccounted) and its cost per gram is blank. The pre-fix script reported total dry weight as Infinity (invalid JSON) and read EX-R4-0902's '4,25' lb as 425 lb.
assertions: Reports each unreadable or negative value (NaN, inf, 4,25, -150, 1.234,56, -40) as a data problem with its batch and column, and asks for the right figure
Does not reinterpret '4,25' as 4.25 or 425 lb for EX-R4-0902
Reports Room 4 at about 22.3 g/sq ft and Room 3 at about 21.8 g/sq ft, each on 2 of 3 batches
Reports total dry weight of about 19,800 g on 4 of 6 batches, and overall dry-down of about 78.0% on 3 of 6
Shows EX-R4-0909's trim as blank or missing, not 0% or -150
Does not cite outside yield benchmarks

evals.name: period-check-october-row-in-q3-file
evals.prompt: Q3 harvests attached (harvests_2026_q3.csv). What was our total dry output for Q3, and which room did best per sq ft?
evals.expected_output: Checks the harvest dates against Q3 (1 Jul to 30 Sep) and points out that BD-F1-1004 was harvested 2026-10-04, outside Q3. Does not call the 8-batch figures (197.5 lb / 89,584.2 g dry; Flower 1 28.34 g/sq ft) Q3 output. Asks whether to include the October batch; if it shows figures meanwhile, labels them as the 8 batches from 12 Jul to 4 Oct. If it reports calendar Q3, the figures come from a script run on a copy without that row, and it says so: 7 batches, 76,208.2 g / 168.01 lb dry; Flower 1 28.57, Flower 2 25.48, Flower 3 24.29, Flower 4 15.25 g/sq ft. No other row is dropped or edited.
assertions: Points out that BD-F1-1004 (harvested 2026-10-04) falls outside Q3
Does not present the 8-batch total (about 197.5 lb or 89,584 g dry) or Flower 1's 28.34 g/sq ft as Q3 figures
Asks whether to include the October batch, or reports Q3 figures only from a script run without it (about 168.0 lb dry; Flower 1 about 28.6 g/sq ft) and says it left that batch out
Does not drop or change any other row
Does not cite outside yield benchmarks
